title: The library and the worn path

data.source: A toy with eight forms (a Polya urn against a fixed library), from check F4 of Phoenix study FORMS-AND-EASEMENT-2026-10-06, re-run here with a fresh seed.

prediction: If forms are worn in by use, each form that has happened becomes likelier and the next form grows less surprising; a fixed library of forms stays equally surprising for ever. But a library whose weights rise with use makes exactly the same choices as worn paths, so counting forms cannot tell those two apart.
baseline: Lee Smolin's principle of precedence, which Phoenix says is the only version with a prediction of its own, and Michael Levin's Platonic-space proposal in its learning-library form.
